findings.rule: Rule of thumb: judge only a comparable window with known collection coverage.
findings.reason: Performance Schema is off (MariaDB's default); open Server > Instruments for categories and accounts.

findings.rule: Rule of thumb: tracked bytes increased by more than both 1% of the starting total and 16 MiB across the window.
findings.reason: A short allocation burst can be normal; this does not prove a leak.

notes: MariaDB process-list memory covers visible sessions; without PROCESS, only this user's sessions are visible.

MariaDB Memory_used counts only allocations made through the server's own allocator (my_malloc), so most InnoDB memory, the buffer pool included, is missing. Categories, accounts and a global high-water mark are not collected.
Tracked allocations are not process RSS or machine RAM; no RAM capacity is inferred.
Each event high is an upper bound (current bytes plus per-thread, account and host headroom), not a recorded peak; their sum is not a server peak.
Enabled instruments do not recover earlier allocations; session/account totals need not add up to the global total.
Categories use known event-name prefixes; unmatched allocations stay in Other, and TempTable may include mapped files.
Reads are sequential, not an atomic snapshot; the collection itself can allocate memory.
